messages.subject: the index of association
parts:
Hello,

I was testing the index of association, and I got this. The rbarD is way off and the P.rD is 1. Does this mean there's significant linkage disequilibrium? And that the population might be clonal?


      Ia       p.Ia      rbarD       p.rD 
-0.3126761  0.8330000 -0.1826554  1.0000000

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] the index of association
parts:
Hi Jennifer,

The simulation study I performed for the final chapter in my dissertation actually touched on this very topic [0]. In short, negative values of the index of association with high p-values are an anomaly caused by low allelic diversity and high evenness. Basically, highly negative values reflect a limitation of the index of association and should be treated with caution. You can see this in effect with the HunterCr_OR population of the Pram (Phytophthora ramorum) data set embedded in poppr:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("poppr"))
data(Pram)
ia(Pram[pop = "HunterCr_OR"], sample = 999, plot = FALSE)
#>          Ia        p.Ia       rbarD        p.rD 
#> -0.04399111  0.79100000 -0.04708428  1.00000000
locus_table(Pram, pop = "HunterCr_OR")
#> 
#> allele = Number of observed alleles
#> 1-D = Simpson index
#> Hexp = Nei's 1978 gene diversity
#> ------------------------------------------
#>           summary
#> locus      allele  1-D Hexp Evenness
#>   PrMS6A1    2.00 0.50 0.50     1.00
#>   Pr9C3A1    2.00 0.50 0.50     1.00
#>   PrMS39A1   3.00 0.54 0.54     0.89
#>   PrMS45A1   2.00 0.50 0.50     1.00
#>   PrMS43A1   4.00 0.51 0.52     0.91
#>   mean       2.60 0.51 0.51     0.96
I would recommend to assess different pieces of evidence for clonality. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian


[0] So you don't have to read all 50 (thesis) pages of it, here's the conclusion about negative values: https://zkamvar.github.io/dissertation/5-factors-influencing-inference-of-clonality-in-diploid-populations.html#allelic-diversity-influences-the-value-of-barr_d-in-clonal-populations
